title: A missing/invalid API key on any eagerly-validating cloud provider (OpenAI, Groq, and by shared-class construction OpenRouter/xAI/DeepSeek) now surfaces the router's generic 'The terminal hit an internal error... restart Vysted' frame instead of a humanized 'add your API key in Settings' message, on both /agents/{id}/invoke and /llm/chat
repro: python3 scripts/r15/vy.py invoke copilot "hi" --port 52320 --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --mode agent --autonomy ask --no-key -> SSE {"kind":"error","message":"The terminal hit an internal error.","action":"Try again; if it keeps happening, restart Vysted.","detail":"OpenAIError: Missing credentials...","code":"internal"}. Reproduced identically for provider=groq (GroqError: api_key client option must be set...) and via a direct curl to /llm/chat for provider=openai. Provider=anthropic on the SAME /llm/chat route correctly humanizes to {message:'Something went wrong with Anthropic.', action:'Try again or switch provider in Settings.', code:'unknown'} because Anthropic's SDK defers key validation to request time, while OpenAI's/Groq's SDK client constructor raises immediately.
suspected_files: sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:591 (client = self._client(api_key) called before the try: at :651, so a client-construction OpenAIError never reaches this adapter's own try/except or humanize())
sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py, sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py (same shape but their SDKs do not raise eagerly, so they are not currently exposed by this gap)
sidecar/routers/agents.py:106-110 (except Exception: yield error_frame(exc) unconditionally, never tries humanize(provider_id, exc) first)

sidecar/services/errors.py:552-568 (error_frame() is hardcoded generic 'internal' by design per R15-AGENT-030's fix_shape, on the premise that 'adapters already humanize their own failures' before reaching the router guard — that premise is false for this call path)
